speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. To determine the cause, is your baby feeding well, and have you noticed any stool that is pale or gray in color?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Hyperbilirubinemia (likely breast milk jaundice). The increasing yellow discoloration in a 2-week-old exclusively breastfed infant is consistent with this common diagnosis, which typically presents after the first week and is associated with inadequate intake or breast milk factors.
